headline_marked: ACC [[sends letters to 41 banks]] over ৳276 crore embezzlement case
headline: ACC sends letters to 41 banks over ৳276 crore embezzlement case
summary: The Anti-Corruption Commission has sought information from 41 banks regarding the alleged embezzlement of CSR funds through the Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman Memorial Trust.
details: The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has sent letters to 41 scheduled banks in Bangladesh to gather information for a case involving the alleged embezzlement of ৳276 crore from Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) funds.

The case names ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina and her sister, Sheikh Rehana, as defendants. Nazrul Islam Majumder, former chairman of Exim Bank and former president of the Bangladesh Association of Banks (BAB), is also listed as an accused.
According to the FIR, Sheikh Hasina served as the president of the Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman Memorial Trust, and Sheikh Rehana was the vice-president.
The FIR further alleges that the two sisters used the Trust to collect funds from banks' CSR funds for 'dishonest purposes of personal gain' by exercising influence through the BAB.
The ACC is currently reviewing records and information obtained from these 41 scheduled banks to further the investigation into the funds' movement and usage.
caption:
৳276 crore embezzled from bank CSR funds? The ACC is now investigating 41 banks.

The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has sent letters to 41 scheduled banks in Bangladesh to gather information for a case involving the alleged embezzlement of ৳276 crore from Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) funds.

The case names ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina and her sister, Sheikh Rehana, as defendants. Nazrul Islam Majumder, former chairman of Exim Bank and former president of the Bangladesh Association of Banks (BAB), is also listed as an accused.

According to the FIR, Sheikh Hasina served as the president of the Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman Memorial Trust, and Sheikh Rehana was the vice-president.

The FIR further alleges that the two sisters used the Trust to collect funds from banks' CSR funds for 'dishonest purposes of personal gain' by exercising influence through the BAB.

The ACC is currently reviewing records and information obtained from these 41 scheduled banks to further the investigation into the funds' movement and usage.

Source: Jamuna TV
